newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Oil price hike puts Asian trading in deep freeze.
newsitem.headline: Oil price hike puts Asian trading in deep freeze.

text.p: Crude oil prices skyrocketed in Asia after the United States launched a missile attack on Iraq, bringing physical buying to a standstill and hurting the share prices of Chinese oil refineries in Hong Kong.

In Singapore, Asia's oil trading hub, physical oil trading came to a standstill Tuesday after the benchmark Brent futures contract on the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) jumped to US$23.50 per barrel after opening at $22.90.
"There are no physical transactions. The market has frozen and players are not willing to do anything. They are just waiting to see what happens," said a Singapore-based trading manager by telephone.

"Our refiners simply cannot absorb current international prices. If this problem persists, it would definately affect our imports," a source at China's key crude oil trader Unipec told Reuters by phone, adding that crude oil imports would become prohibitive at $22.00 per barrel on delivered basis.

Refineries in China, a huge crude oil buyer in Asia, have long been protected by artificially low domestic crude oil prices. Coastal refiners that import crude are usually stung badly when international prices rise.
